description: Team di Antonio Barbarisi e Diego Forcellati.
summary: Earth System Trend Detective! is a web app that helps determine whether a change observed by satellites is a genuine trend or merely noise. On an interactive global map, users can select a variable—such as GISTEMP temperature anomalies or the NDVI vegetation index—and choose a specific grid cell. The app then generates an annual time series, calculates the Sen’s slope per decade and the Mann-Kendall p-value, and provides a verdict in plain language—all processed directly within the browser. Users can also analyze their own data: the "Data Builder" tool allows for the input of coordinates, the pasting or importing of annual time series (in CSV or JSON format), and the calculation of Sen’s slope and p-values ​​for each data point using the same methodology applied to the map. The resulting `dati_trend.json` file can be downloaded or loaded directly back onto the map. A Python pipeline handles the preparation of NASA NetCDF data. The project also features illustrative case studies (covering the Arctic, the Sahel, the Amazon, and an example with no discernible trend), a guide to the methodology, citable NASA sources, and a section on environmental and human impacts. Available in eight languages ​​and offering both light and dark themes, the platform makes trend analysis reproducible and accessible to students, the general public, and policymakers—not just experts.
details: Earth System Trend Detective! was created to bridge the gap between the complexity of raw geospatial data and its practical usability. Technically, the platform is built on a lightweight, high-performance architecture using HTML5, Tailwind CSS, and native JavaScript, integrating advanced libraries such as Leaflet.js for interactive global mapping and Chart.js for the dynamic visualization of time series. The project’s true innovative core lies in its analytical engine: the application processes official satellite datasets (such as GISTEMPv4 for temperatures and NDVI for vegetation) through a rigorous statistical pipeline. This includes removing monthly climatology to neutralize seasonal cycles, performing the non-parametric Mann-Kendall test, and calculating the Theil-Sen slope. This combination allows for the mathematical separation of genuine climate trends from background noise, eliminating distortions caused by anomalous individual years and providing definitive assessments of statistical significance. From a creative and design perspective, the team opted for an immersive interface styled as an "investigative dossier," featuring a polished design, native support for both dark and light modes, and fluid navigation. The experience is rounded out by a custom dataset builder and a section dedicated to ecological impact and CO₂ emissions. Hosted live on InfinityFree, the platform combines scientific rigor with open-science transparency, offering the jury a comprehensive, original, and immediately applicable tool for the ecological transition.
